newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks fall 7.45pct after frantic selling.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks fall 7.45pct after frantic selling.

text.p: Athens equities dropped 7.45 percent on Monday and fund managers said they expected the bourse to be weak in the short term and consolidate in the medium term.
"Bourse sentiment has deteriorated. There was selling panic and no buying interest today," said Yanna Tziovara, an assistant portfolio manager at Allianz Mutual Funds.
The rise of the general index by almost 50 percent from the beginning of January until the last week of February was very sharp and a correction was in the cards, said Tziovara.
"The selling climate was initiated by retail investors who were in for short-term profits. The fact that they acted massively, caused panic in the bourse," she said.
Tziovara said she expected the general share index to fall to 950-1,000 points in the short-run.
"If the market then manages to consolidate at 1,100 points for one or two months it could start rising again but at a slower pace," she said.
Other fund managers said predictions about the short-term course of the bourse was unfounded.

"The market sentiment is negative. But this is not justified because macroeconomic figures have not changed," said John Glykos, an assistant fund manager at Doriki Mutual Funds. "However, I expect a recovery in the medium-term."
Investors should learn to react calmly to various statements, he added.
"It was not so much Thomadakis' fault as it was the investors' reaction to his statement. They should not be influenced by such comments," said Glykos.
The Athens general share index closed 7.45 percent down or 97.09 points lower at 1206.54 from Friday's 1303.63, after opening at 1291.09.
Turnover was 16.7 billion drachmas on volume of 4.8 million shares. Decliners led advancers 222 to 19 with 5 issues unchanged on 246 issues traded.
Sectoral indices were down, with big losses incurred in construction and banking shares, down 7.98 and 7.72 percent respectively. Industrials lost 7.54 percent and small-caps ended 2.86 percent down.
Leasing shares ended 7.30 percent weaker and investment shares closed 7.65 percent down. Insurance stocks settled 3.24 percent lower.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 913.00-941.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, were trading 400 drachmas lower at 5,400.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 9,064-9,541 drachmas.
